items.title: Inside the Suns: Defense, Defense, Defense!
items.content:
Welcome to Inside the Suns, your weekly deep-down analysis of the current Phoenix Suns team. Each week, the Fantable — a round table of Bright Siders — gives their takes on the Suns’ latest issues and news.

Fantable Questions of the WeekQ1: The Suns finished last season 10th in defensive rating.  Do you believe they will be better, worse, or about the same defensively in 2026-27?GuarGuar: I think overall we will be around the same defensively, maybe slightly better overall with our rating. 10th is pretty good overall, so it’s not really a big problem if we finish the same. However, we were really streaky defensively last year, and I’d rather we be consistently around 10 all year than 6 for half the season and 18ish for the other half…as was the case last season. More minutes for Fleming and Maluach should help us defensively, and I expect Ott to play fewer small-ball lineups this season.

zenzino: I knew this set of questions was coming when grey_hound asked, “What happened to defense? All the answers seemed focused on offense,” and Keratosis concurred, saying many were guilty of that. In another part, Rod said he’d been going easy on us. I said, “Bring it!” And it’s been brought.

I can’t speak for anyone else, but my lineup ideas took defense into account. The reason it “seems” like the focus is on offense is that I’m not worried about defense. The grit and tenacity that last season’s Suns built their reputation on were largely about playing defense for 48 minutes. The foundation this coaching staff preaches is getting more offensive possessions on the defensive side of the ball.

I believe the Suns will be a little better on defense this year. Whether that translates to them moving up in the ranking or not depends on other teams.

Because of injuries and other factors, the Suns slid a little in the second half of the season. If they stay healthy, I don’t see that slide happening again.

This is also where the continuity comes in. Team defense, way more than offense, takes time and chemistry to develop. This is why (in addition to players wanting to show out) you don’t see any team defense in All-Star games and not much in Summer League. It takes time to learn those defensive schemes and learn the strengths and habits (good and bad) of your teammates.

I don’t think the Bridges trade necessarily made them better on defense, but it didn’t make them worse, either. Sheer and Man Man getting more experience will give them additional defensive length as well.

So, yeah…I definitely expect them to be in the top 10 and maybe move closer to 5 than 10.

Ashton: Well, shame on me for not realizing that the Suns finished 10th out of thirty teams. That isn’t bad. Also, I am just not a huge fan of defensive metrics, but a few commentators got up in arms about the lack of defense articles. So, what does Rod do? Dump the whole thing on the Fantable.

To me, defensive ratings are complicated and not the first stat I run to after the game. This is the formula.

items.title: Seven First-Timers Highlight USA's Women's World Cup Roster
items.content:
USA Basketball finalized its 12-player roster for the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, set to run Sept. 4-13, with seven players set to make their World Cup debuts. Aliyah Boston, Paige Bueckers, Caitlin Clark, Napheesa Collier, Rhyne Howard, Angel Reese and Jackie Young will all appear in the tournament for the first time, joined by veterans Kahleah Copper, Chelsea Gray, Kelsey Plum, Breanna Stewart and A'ja Wilson.

Stewart will become just the third player in national team history to appear in at least four World Cups, joining Sue Bird, who has five, and Diana Taurasi, who has four. She is the only New York Liberty player on the roster, with teammate Sabrina Ionescu notably left off.

"We'll probably have more than half of our team going to the World Cup," said Stewart, addressing the number of Liberty players expected to compete internationally.

The roster collectively holds 14 Olympic gold medals and nine World Cup titles. USA Basketball women's national team managing director Sue Bird praised the group in a statement.

"This is an incredibly talented group that has earned the opportunity to compete in Berlin," said Bird. "Wearing a USA jersey is a privilege, and I know these 12 players will embrace that responsibility as we go after another gold medal. I can't wait to see what this team accomplishes together."

Bird was named the program's first managing director last May and has overseen coaching staff and roster selections heading into the 2028 Olympic cycle, with her choices approved by the USA Basketball Board of Governors. Duke head coach Kara Lawson will lead the team, assisted by Golden State Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase, Phoenix Mercury coach Nate Tibbetts and Indiana Fever coach Stephanie White. Dallas Wings coach Jose Fernandez and Duke assistant Tia Jackson will serve as scout coaches.

Lawson addressed the difficulty of narrowing the roster to 12 players.

"It's been a long process to whittle it down to 12 players, and I think that speaks to just the talent we have in our country across the board," said Lawson. "These 12 have earned it through their play and their consistency. I couldn't be more excited about working with each of them, and I've had a good experience with each of them."

The U.S. enters the tournament as the defending champion, having won its fourth consecutive World Cup gold medal in 2022 with an 83-61 win over China in the final. 

The WNBA season will pause from Aug. 31 to Sept. 16 to accommodate the tournament, with the Liberty resuming their regular-season schedule Sept. 18 against the Minnesota Lynx. Stewart addressed the quick turnaround between competitions.

"It's really not that many days of practice," said Stewart. "Going against the best teams in the world is no joke. I think the World Cup is the harder competition between that and the Olympics just from a schedule standpoint. When we get together, we'll be ready."

items.title: And-Ones: Basketball Without Borders, FAs, Rozier, Schedule
items.content:
Current NBA players Brook Lopez (Clippers), Khris Middleton (Wizards), and Jalen Suggs (Magic) are among the individiuals who will serve as coaches at a Basketball Without Borders Next Up camp in Istanbul, Türkiye later this month, the league announced in a press release.

Cavaliers head coach Kenny Atkinson and former NBA players Vlade Divac and Danilo Gallinari will also be involved in guiding 80 top international high-school age prospects through the event, which will include “athletic testing, movement efficiency, skill development stations, 3-on-3 competitions, life-skills seminars, and 5-on-5 games.”

We have more from around the basketball world:

Eric Pincus of Bleacher Report checks in on several of the top free agents left on the open market, exploring why Jonathan Kuminga, DeMar DeRozan, Russell Westbrook, and James Harden are still unsigned and when – and how – that might change. Pincus also takes a look at the three remaining restricted free agents, suggesting that the most likely outcome for Jalen Duren, Peyton Watson, and Bennedict Mathurin is returning to their respective teams. Of the three, Pincus views Mathurin as the best candidate to relocate.
Federal prosecutors have accused Deniro Laster – a childhood friend and co-defendant of Terry Rozier in the ongoing NBA gambling case – of attempting to tamper with a witness, according to Tom Schad of ESPN. Those prosecutors have alleged that Laster has attempted to contact his co-defendants directly and through intermediaries and that he has posted rat emojis on Instagram at least twice with intent to intimidate, arguing that he has “repeatedly and flagrantly violated the conditions of his release.” They’ve asked a judge to revoke his bond and hold him custody until the trial, which is scheduled to begin on February 8.
The NBA’s schedule release for the 2026/27 season isn’t far off. According to Marc Stein of The Stein Line (Twitter link), the expectation is that the league will reveal its regular season schedule at some point next week.
